newsitem.title: USA: U.S. group says few cars have good head restraints.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group says few cars have good head restraints.

text.p: A Honda Motor Co. Ltd. Civic, a Mercedes Benz, a Toyota Motor Corp. Supra and two Volvos are the only 1997 cars with good head restraints to protect against whiplash and other neck injuries, a safety group said on Tuesday.

The industry-backed Insurance Institute for Highway Safety said that more than half of all 1997 passenger cars tested have poor restraints and fewer than three percent have restraint designs with good geometry.
It said that dozens of cars have restraints that are neither high enough nor close enough to the back of the head to have the potential to protect many people in rear-end collisions.
"A sad showing," said institute president Brian O'Neill. "This issue hasn't been a priority among automakers."
"It's a situation that needs to change," he said, "because to have a good head restraint design, good geometry is a necessary first step."

The institute said good geometry for restraints, required on cars since 1969, means they should be as high as the top of the occupant's head and with as little distance as possible between them and the back of the occupant's head.
It said the backsets of more than four inches have been associated with increased symptoms of neck injury.

The institute said the only vehicles with restraints it considered "good" were the Honda Civic del Sol and the Mercedes E class, both with restaints that adjust automatically, the Toyota Supra and two Volvo models, the 850 and 960.
Others restraints were rated acceptable, marginal or poor.
